why: Travel decisions are made on feeling. A vertical film of the suite they booked or the plates leaving the pass triggers telepresence — the cognitive sensation of already being in the room. The guest starts mentally rehearsing the stay, which drops travel anxiety and raises booking excitement.

Travelers are skeptical of polished static photography and assume the crop is hiding a highway or a dated lobby. Real-time visual proof of the actual property bypasses that suspicion entirely, and trust is the currency conversion runs on.
Putting your own team on camera turns operational staff into the faces of the brand. That builds internal pride, and pride shows up as white-glove service on the lobby floor.

Most travel sharing happens in private channels — WhatsApp, DMs, SMS. A custom film welcoming a guest by name gets forwarded into group chats to show off the upcoming trip, which is word of mouth arriving unpaid.
